## Biological Narrative

The differential metabolite profile is most strongly indicative of a coordinated xenobiotic biotransformation response. RaMP enrichment identified **Phase I - Functionalization of compounds** and **Phase II - Conjugation of compounds** as the top-ranked Reactome pathways, with fold enrichments of 137.2 and 178.9 respectively, together covering nine of the ten input compounds. A broader parent pathway, **Biological oxidations**, had a fold enrichment of 148.7 and captured nine matched compounds.

**Phase II - Conjugation of compounds** is driven by five matched compounds: benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853), N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319), 6-methylmercaptopurine (C16614), beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928), and glutathione (C00051). Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl are Phase II substrates for glutathione conjugation, indicating the treatment generates reactive aromatic intermediates captured by this pathway. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide is also a confirmed member of **Glutathione conjugation**.

**Phase I - Functionalization of compounds** is dominated by coumarin (C05851), 3-aminopropionaldehyde (C05665), methimazole (C07190), and bromide (C01324). These reflect oxidative xenobiotic metabolism; coumarin is a classic CYP450 probe substrate and methimazole is a known flavin-monooxygenase substrate.

**Biological significance:** The convergence of aromatic carcinogen metabolites (C14853, C20319), thiol-conjugating agents (C00051, C00928, C16614), and Phase I probe substrates (C05851, C07190) is characteristic of exposure to electrophilic pollutants such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, triggering a dual-phase detoxification response centered on oxidative biotransformation and glutathione conjugation.
